details: Several major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada, European Central Bank (ECB), and Bank of Japan, are scheduled to announce their latest policy decisions this week. The US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is set for October 27-28, with its interest rate decision and Chair's press conference on October 28. These decisions, alongside upcoming US inflation and GDP data, are crucial as markets anticipate potential shifts in monetary policy that could impact global financial markets and risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Central Banks Set to Announce Key Policy Decisions This Week

details: On October 26, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) encouraged community banks to become permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act. This landmark move provides a regulated pathway for banks to issue dollar-denominated payment stablecoins, establishing clear rules for reserve assets, redemption obligations, risk management, and audits. This development aims to integrate traditional banking with on-chain payment rails, potentially fostering greater institutional adoption of stablecoins.
title: US OCC Encourages Banks to Issue Stablecoins Under GENIUS Act

details: Bitcoin's price slipped below the key $80,000 mark on October 26, reaching its lowest level in over a month following a weekend sell-off. This decline reflects broader market caution driven by rising oil prices, persistent inflation concerns, and uncertainty ahead of the US Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decision. Heavy outflows from spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and liquidations in futures markets further intensified selling pressure across the cryptocurrency market.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80,000 Amid Macroeconomic Uncertainty

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) submitted a response to the European Commission's targeted review of the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation on September 22, 2026. The ECB recommended replacing the fixed deposit floors for stablecoins, citing concerns about contagion risk. The central bank highlighted that a large stablecoin deposit base could create an unstable funding source for host banks, potentially transmitting stress from the token market to the banking system during mass redemptions.
title: ECB Recommends Changes to MiCA Stablecoin Deposit Rules
